human_tolerance.notes: Synanthropic and closely associated with people: it builds its clay oven on trees, fence posts, telephone poles and buildings, so a garden or patio almost always has a pair.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: 'The rufous hornero breeds in the austral summer, laying eggs between August and December'; the exact phase boundaries are a judgement around that range.

vocalizations.description: A loud, far-carrying dawn song of repeated harsh notes, given from a high perch on a tree, post or wire; the song is the usual way a pair announces a defended territory.
A sharp, repeated metallic call given when a bird is disturbed at the nest or on the ground.

taxonomy.note: Rank and accepted name from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy; the species is currently placed in Furnarius.

external.note: GBIF usage key from the GBIF Backbone match for the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id and Wikidata Q-id from Wikidata.

conservation.note: The article's taxobox gives the IUCN status as LC.

range.note: 'Its range includes midwestern, southeastern, and southern Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northern and central Argentina, extending as far south as northern Patagonia.' Country list is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form of that sentence.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Rufous horneros feed on insects and other arthropods obtained by foraging on the ground while walking', so the ground gait is Walk; the bird also flies strongly and directly. Hopping, climbing and swimming are not described.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The nest of the species is typical for the genus, a large thick clay "oven" placed on a tree, or man-made structures such as fence posts, telephone poles, or buildings.' The oven is a closed chamber entered through a side hole, which is what the schema calls a cavity.

traits.perching.note: Both articles describe the bird perching on posts, wires, poles and branches to sing and to work on the nest.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits 1.0 BirdFuncDat row for Furnarius rufus: BodyMass-Value 46.42 g.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'a medium-sized ovenbird at 18 to 20 centimetres (7-8 in) and 31 to 58 grams (1.1-2.05 oz), with males being heavier.'

traits.wingspan_m.note: Neither Wikipedia article states a wingspan. Derived from the stated wing length of 10.2 cm ('Wings length is 10.2 centimetres') at about 2.1x, the usual span-to-single-wing ratio for a medium passerine, giving about 0.21 m. This is an approximation, not a sourced figure.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No open-licensed source gives a typical or maximum lifespan for Furnarius rufus: the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles, Wikidata and GBIF carry none, and the field-guide and Animal Diversity Web pages were avoided under the licence policy. 5.0 years is a documented judgement placeholder, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Diet-Inv 80, Diet-Seed 20 (BirdFuncDat row for Furnarius rufus, Diet-Certainty A). The article's 'slender and slightly decurved bill suited to eating insects' is consistent with the invertebrate share.

traits.social.note: 'The species is monogamous and the pair bond is long-term, sometimes for life... Pairs remain together throughout the year.' group_size is fixed at the pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Nocturnal 0; both articles describe daytime foraging and the dawn song.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flushes from the ground to a perch when approached, the escape the shared perching-songbird program encodes.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from the described closeness to people: it nests on buildings, fence posts and telephone poles and is described as synanthropic, so it tolerates close approach.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Rests and sleeps in the clay oven nest or in a tree cavity.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate and seed weights follow the EltonTraits diet shares; cavity nesting and the perch/platform tags follow the described nest sites ('on a tree, or man-made structures such as fence posts, telephone poles, or buildings').

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and road_mortality from the described nesting on buildings and structures; light_max is a judgement, since no night activity is described.

seasonal.strategy.note: The pair holds territory and works on the nest year-round, with breeding confined to the austral summer.

seasonal.phases.note: 'The rufous hornero breeds in the austral summer, laying eggs between August and December' gives the window; the exact phase boundaries are a judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'The eggs are laid every second day and incubated for 14-18 days. Chicks are fed for 23-26 days before fledging; young birds remain in the parental territory for around 6 months after fledging.' duration_days is incubation plus nestling time, taken at the midpoints (16 + 24.5 days, rounded to 62 including the laying interval), and scale is a judgement for a recently fledged bird.

vocalizations.song.note: The article describes the male's loud song from a perch and the article carries a recording of the species' calls; the description is written from the article's account of the song.

vocalizations.alarm.note: The article's audio file is captioned 'Alarm call'.

look.note: Rufous-brown upperparts, pale buff throat and breast, a brighter rufous tail, a slender slightly decurved bill and dark grey bill and legs; the Spanish article adds a pale supercilium. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. It is the best fit of the four shared programs because the article describes the bird foraging on the ground while walking, which is exactly what the program animates, and the program can rest it in the oven while the sun is up. The limitation to note in the pull request: this program has no song state, so the hornero's loud dawn song - its best-known behaviour - is not represented, and a bespoke program was not written for it.
